sample_unit: community respondent survey sets (27 ChatGPT, 20 Gemini)

links.outcome: Physician-rated failure of LLM answers to address urgent symptoms warranting referral
links.effect: Physicians reported answers failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
links.quote: Physicians evaluating the same LLM outputs reported the answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%) and failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).

links.outcome: Physician-rated omission of recent advances and research in LLM answers
links.effect: Answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%).
links.quote: Physicians evaluating the same LLM outputs reported the answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%) and failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).

links.outcome: LLM omission of risks and of when to seek professional care, alongside high perceived quality
links.effect: Failed to address risks of mentioned procedures/medications (ChatGPT 38%, Gemini 28.6%); omitted when to consult professional (ChatGPT 27.2%, Gemini 40.8%); respondents rated quality similar or better than physicians.
links.quote: The LLMs failed to address potential risks for procedures and medications it mentioned (ChatGPT 38%, Gemini 28.6%).

screen.reason: Empirical survey and expert evaluation of LLM-generated patient health information regarding Moyamoya disease, assessing safety, omissions, and user perception without testing a deployment practice.
